Saga's Chicago study 1 estimated that offering tutoring increased participation by 0.563 years.
Saga's Chicago study 1 estimated that offering tutoring increased participation for at least one year by 42.3 percentage points.
Saga's Chicago study 1 estimated that offering tutoring increased participation for two years by 13.9 percentage points.
Saga's Chicago study 1 estimated a year-two CPS math test (study sample Z) effect of 0.228 study-sample standard deviations per year of tutoring.
Saga's Chicago study 1 reported a year-two bound of 0.835 study-sample standard deviations for CPS math test (study sample Z), assuming only two-year participation contributes.
Saga's Chicago study 1 estimated a year-two Math GPA effect of 0.180 GPA points per year of tutoring.
Saga's Chicago study 1 reported a year-two bound of 0.243 GPA points for Math GPA, assuming only first-year benefits persist.
Saga's Chicago study 1 reported a year-two bound of 0.630 GPA points for Math GPA, assuming only two-year participation contributes.
Saga's Chicago study 1 estimated 8.0 percentage points fewer math courses failed per year of tutoring, measured in year two.
Saga's Chicago study 1 reported a 10.9-percentage-point bound on reducing math-course failure, assuming only first-year benefits persist.
Saga's Chicago study 1 reported a 28.1-percentage-point bound on reducing math-course failure, assuming only two-year participation contributes.
